WORKLOG / DOSSIER - payment_plans task 0 (root: plans_ext_added_invoice_installment) - revision 2

0. DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0028_clinical_laboratory_company/tasks/payment_plans --task 0):
{"task": 0, "key": "env_0028_clinical_laboratory_company/payment_plans/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 5, 6]}
Counts: added-invoice installment (root) 6, relief installment 6, add-on down payment 5, catch-up payment 4. Task 1 draws 1 prerequisite problem, counts [4, 6].

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The caller asks only to put her new lab bill (invoice 42190644) on her existing plan. The records show (a) the plan is past due (installment 8 recorded missed 2026-10-06), so its schedule may not change until it is brought current by the patient's own catch-up payment; (b) a financial-assistance release of 1,120.00 was booked 2026-10-02 but the installment is still the acceptance installment 185.00, so a relief installment is owed; (c) adding an invoice to an accepted 18-Month plan (a term with a down payment) carries an add-on down payment paid by the patient. Each of the four amounts is a multi-factor computation over the plan ledger, the assistance file, the coverage file and the invoice record; one tool per problem, so nothing is gained by guessing tools.

2. SCOPE. First task. Claimed: plans_ext_catch_up_payment (pay_catch_up_2a071954, user), plans_ext_relief_installment (reset_relief_installment_53948494), plans_ext_add_on_down_payment (pay_add_on_down_payment_958d6e13, user), plans_ext_added_invoice_installment (add_invoice_to_plan_14a3a600). Task 1 keeps the defaulted-plan path (reinstatement payment and reinstatement). Acceptance and cancellation are not used (their events trigger into the invoices category).

3. BASE LINEAGE AND OVERRIDES. catch-up: refs plans_evt_installments (payable_plan inherited), plans_evt_delinquency; overwrite of the partial-payment sentence 'A payment below the installment due counts toward it only when partial_installment_accepted is true; otherwise it is applied as extra principal and the installment is still owed.' -> only extra-principal payments posted against the latest missed installment (carrying its installment number) count toward the catch-up; payments carrying no installment number keep the base treatment (they reduce the balance without moving the schedule). The cure sentence 'It becomes current again only when every past-due installment is paid in full' holds: the credited payments plus the catch-up settle installment 8 in full. add-on: refs plans_evt_installments, plans_term_selection_and_terms; overwrite []. relief: refs plans_evt_schedule_changes (change_active_only), plans_evt_release_and_assistance; overwrite of 'the installment is recomputed over the remaining installments when assistance_adjustment_reamortizes is true'. root: refs plans_agg_invoice_consolidation, plans_evt_invoice_eligibility, plans_evt_release_and_assistance; overwrite of the re-amortize/extension clause. Every rule states its rounding: to the nearest cent, an exact half cent rounded up; no computed value of this world (gold, factor substitutions, fall-backs) lands on an exact half cent.

4. FACTOR CARD (tier taken; result under the factor's baseline).
catch-up (gold 110.00; whole baseline 185.00):
 - catch_up_credit_selection [method: which payments posted against the missed installment are counted - largest single / most recent / all]: 2 missed lines in 12 months + bank draws -> the largest, 75.00 (of 75.00 on 10-09 and 40.00 on 10-12); baseline all 115.00 -> 92.50. Near-miss: 40.00 of 08-10 and 125.00 of 05-29 carry no installment number (posted while current) and never count.
 - catch_up_credit_share [parameter, cross-difficulty assistance CFIELD household_size]: approved award + household 3 -> whole; baseline one half -> 147.50.
 - catch_up_credit_cap [parameter]: 6 scheduled installments in 12 months -> cap one half installment 92.50 (not binding); baseline one quarter 46.25 binds -> 138.75.
 - catch_up_minimum [parameter]: autopay, accepted 9 months ago -> 46.25; baseline one installment -> 185.00.
 Installment 3's missed line is settled on the ledger by an arrears payment (2026-05-08), so every reading of the rule leaves it out of the amount owed; no factor draws weight from it.
relief installment (gold 35.00; whole baseline 55.00): award months 1, document months 1, standing months 1 (6 scheduled in 12 months), coverage months 1 (cross-difficulty coverage), invoice months 1 -> count 15, each baseline (0) -> 37.50; relief_floor [method] 15 percent of 185.00 = 27.75, baseline term minimum 55.00 -> 55.00.
add-on down payment (gold 9.50; whole baseline 36.48): rate 5 percent (cross-difficulty assistance) -> baseline 10 percent 19.00; class one half -> 19.00; add_on_missed_raise [method: latest-only / compounding / step] bank-drawn with 6 scheduled -> x 1.25 although 2 missed lines lie in the last 12 months, baseline step x 1.5 -> 11.40; invoice count x 1.25 -> 7.60; minimum 5.00 -> 25.00.
added-invoice installment (gold 51.69; whole baseline 43.75): folding layered -> baseline re-spread 70.00 (capped); count reading 525.00 / 35.00 = 15 -> baseline term count 60.97; spread cap 18 -> baseline 9 64.21; netting all of 9.50 -> baseline none 52.37; held installments 1 -> baseline none 50.58; rise cap double -> baseline 25 percent 43.75.
Every baseline is what the policy's baseline.rule states for that input.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. State gates only: payable_plan for the two user payments (past_due / active), change_active_only for the relief installment (active after the catch-up, whose tool performs the cure transition), invoice_open and plan_open_for_enrollment for the addition (invoice 42190644 open, balance 243.20, eligible class; plan active), add_invoice_allowed true, 3 invoices <= 10, new balance <= 4,500.00. No time gate.

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Plan 5723e3e9-da84-45ec-9273-a59db2936deb; invoice added ebef2c60-3c72-4c64-8928-b48914f4ecd4 (42190644), open, balance 243.20 after its 243.20 assistance adjustment, claim C4180027316 fully adjudicated. Ledger: enrollments 3,700.00; payments 1,945.00 (down payment 370.00, six scheduled 1,110.00, arrears for installment 3 185.00, extra principal 280.00); release 1,120.00; missed installments 3 (settled) and 8 (unpaid). Only the two October payments carry installment number 8.

7. ROWS. Every plan row enters a sum, count, selection or the carried balance; invoices, invoice activity, orders and claim lines fix the added invoice's final balance and class and explain why the award reached only two invoices; coverage and assistance rows decide the cross-difficulty tiers. plan_balance equals the ledger (635.00). No automatic clause fires on 2026-10-14 (installment 9 falls due 2026-10-20; one unpaid missed installment, default needs 3).

8. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root -> relief installment (value_input, gate n_inst, ACTION form with fallback: the reset leaves only the installment figure, no dated ledger line); root -> add-on down payment (value_input, gate n_addon_down, STATE: a down payment dated after acceptance); relief -> catch-up (value_input, gate c_carried, STATE, negated: an arrears payment dated on or after the latest missed line; the only such writer on a past-due plan is the catch-up). Opening falsity: installment 185.00 = acceptance installment with the release present; only down payment dated the acceptance day; latest missed line 2026-10-06 with the only arrears payment dated 2026-05-08. Order: catch-up -> {relief, add-on} -> root; relief and add-on commute (same values 35.00 / 9.50, identical terminal hash c826a348...). Deletion runs: skip relief -> root 210.97; skip add-on -> root 52.37; skip catch-up -> relief 42.33, root 48.75. Persona names none of these; tools validate none.

9-10. ORDER AND MISTAKES. Doing the root first gives 210.97 or 52.37; mistakes excluded by the rules: crediting the August or May extra principal, counting both October payments, charging installment 3 again, adding the bill at 486.40, ignoring the release, netting nothing, forgetting the held installment, the 10 percent term rate.

11. STANDARD SOLUTION. Locate, verify, read invoices, plan, plan ledger, invoice activity, orders, claim lines, coverages, assistance case and file; hand over the catch-up (installment 8, due 2026-09-20, debit card); set the relief installment; hand over the add-on down payment (debit card); add invoice ebef2c60-3c72-4c64-8928-b48914f4ecd4 at 243.20 with the added-invoice installment.

12. VERIFICATION (revision 2). check_extended, check_task_tools, replay_tasks (closure 45 = 45), check_solvability, check_compute, check_grounding, check_cross_fire: all OK on --task 0 and on the difficulty-wide run. Handling-time values recomputed with the gate's evaluator.

13. SOLVABILITY VS GT. payable_plan (steps 12, 16), change_active_only via prior_step 12 (step 14), invoice_open and plan_open_for_enrollment via prior_step 12 (step 18), consolidation policy_scope.

14. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the rule prose, schemas, lookups and persona: the root's two sentences, the relief sentence and the four computations give the same four writes and values as gold; the ladders are pairwise disjoint and the held-installment sentence now names the method it applies to, so no second reading remains.

15. REVISIONS. Round 1: moved the 40.00 extra principal to 2026-08-10 so the award read bore weight. Round 2 (audit 0.md / _difficulty.md): F1 - the catch-up counted extra principal posted while the plan was current; the credit now counts only payments carrying the latest missed installment's number (the October payments), the overwrite says so, and the August/May payments stay plain extra principal. F2 - the held-installment sentence now applies to the re-spread and states the layering's own treatment (compute unchanged). F3 - the window-length factors were replaced: catch-up credit selection (largest / latest / all) and add-on missed raise (latest-only / compounding / step) are genuine methods; the catch-up gained a credit cap parameter. F5 - installment 3's late payment is booked as the arrears payment it was, so no reading charges it. F4 - every rule states the tie rule and no value of this world is a half-cent tie. O1 - the spread cap's order relative to add-on extension months is stated. O2 - 'approved award' conditions test the award's existence, not a positive discount percentage. O9 - relief_coverage_months declares cross_difficulty coverage. Gates re-run green.
user_scenario:
You are Theresa Sandoval, a 45-year-old from the Rainier Valley in Seattle who worked as a school bus dispatcher until July, calling Halverson Clinical Laboratories' patient line in the middle of a busy morning. You are friendly but a little rushed, you speak in short sentences, and you keep your paperwork in a folder you flip through while you talk.

Why you are calling: a statement arrived for a new bill, invoice number 42190644, for the blood work your doctor ordered back in early September. You already pay Halverson every month on a payment plan for two older lab bills, and you want this new bill put on that same plan so everything comes out of one monthly payment instead of a separate bill. Open with that, in your own words, for example: "I got a new bill from you, invoice 42190644, and I'd like to add it to my payment plan." You are happy for the agent to make the change on your plan for you. Any payment that has to come from you, you will make yourself with your debit card when the agent gives you the way to do it; you never hand over card numbers to the agent.

What you give only when the agent asks: your full name is Theresa Sandoval; your phone number is 2065550147; your date of birth is 1981-07-22; your ZIP code is 98118; your email is theresa.sandoval@outlook.com. If asked what the new bill was for, it was the blood test from about September 2nd. If asked what the statement showed, say the paper statement said $486.40 but you noticed the portal shows less now, so the agent should go by what the system says. If asked about your current monthly payment, you think it is about $185, taken out of your bank account around the 20th, and you want to keep paying that way. If asked whether you applied for financial help, say yes, you applied in August after you lost your job and got a letter in late September saying you were approved; you do not remember the details. If asked about September's payment, say there was a mix-up with your bank account in September, it is sorted out now, and the account is fine for future draws. If asked whether you paid anything toward it since, say you sent $75 online on October 9th and another $40 on October 12th, both by debit card, meaning them for that missed payment; the $40 you sent in August and the $125 from your HSA card in May were just extra toward the balance. You do not know your plan balance, the installment numbers, or any amounts the system would work out, and you never guess them.

How you react: if the agent tells you the plan is behind or that a payment is needed before the new bill can go on, you are a bit embarrassed, say you did not realize, and agree to pay what the agent says is needed. Whenever the agent hands you a payment to make yourself, you make it once, by debit card, for exactly the amount and details the agent tells you, and then you tell the agent it went through. If the agent explains that your monthly payment is being recalculated, or that some amount has to be settled first, you simply say that's fine and to go ahead. If an amount the agent quotes sounds odd to you, you only ask the agent to double-check it against your account; you never suggest a number yourself. You do not ask for anything else: no copy of documents, no change of due date, no other changes.

When the agent confirms the new bill is on your plan and tells you your new monthly payment, thank them, say that works for you, and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's patient profile from the name and phone number she gives, to obtain her customer reference number.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later lookup and every write is keyed to this customer reference number; without it nothing on her plan can be read or changed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify the caller against the profile with two details she states (phone number and date of birth).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identity must be verified before any record is discussed or changed; it is the runtime precondition of every plan write.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her invoices: the two Self-Pay Patient Invoices carried on the plan (status payment_plan) and the new Insured Patient Responsibility Invoice 42190644, open with a balance due of 243.20.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Identifies the invoice to add, confirms it is open (base invoice_open eligibility), and gives the balance due (243.20) and billing class that the add-on down payment and the added-invoice installment are computed from.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her live plan: 18-Month Payment Plan, status past_due, installment 185.00, acceptance down payment 370.00, first due date 2026-02-20, accepted 2026-01-14, automatic draws from a bank account.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The past_due status shows the plan must be brought current before any schedule change or addition; the installment, down payment, first due date, acceptance date and autopay setup feed every one of the four computations.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the whole plan ledger: two enrollments, the acceptance down payment, six scheduled installments, installment 3's missed line (2026-05-06) and the arrears payment that settled it (2026-05-08), four extra-principal payments (125.00 and 40.00 with no installment number, posted while the plan was current; 75.00 and 40.00 posted in October against installment 8), installment 8's missed line (2026-10-06) and the financial-assistance release of 1,120.00 booked 2026-10-02.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The missed lines and payments decide the catch-up payment; the release line shows a relief installment is owed; the carried balance, scheduled-installment count, missed-installment counts and invoice count feed the relief installment, the add-on down payment and the added-invoice installment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the activity on her invoices: the postings and statements, and the financial-assistance adjustments of 1,120.00 on invoice 41728390 and 243.20 on invoice 42190644.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows that the balance due of 243.20 on the new invoice already reflects its assistance adjustment, so the amount carried onto the plan is that balance and not the 486.40 first stated.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the three orders behind her invoices with their collection dates (2025-12-09, 2026-01-06, 2026-09-02) and billing methods.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The collection dates place the new invoice's service inside the award window and the older self-pay invoice outside it, which is why only two invoices show assistance adjustments; it confirms which bill the caller means.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the claim behind the new invoice: filed 2026-09-08, paid 620.80 with a 132.80 contractual adjustment on 2026-09-26 and 486.40 assigned to the patient as deductible on 2026-09-29.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Confirms the claim for the added invoice is fully adjudicated with nothing pending, so its balance due is final and it can join the plan.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her coverage: a live Commercial In-Network Plan (Premera Blue Cross) held through her spouse.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: A live coverage on file sets the coverage extension month of the relief installment and the cap on the rise of the added-invoice installment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read her financial-assistance case: Financial Assistance 50% Discount, approved 2026-09-24, household of 3.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The approved award and its discount percentage and household size decide the catch-up credit span, the add-on down-payment rate, the relief extension months and floor, the spread cap and the rise cap.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the assistance file: pay stubs, an unemployment benefit statement and a tax return received 2026-08-25, and the two discounts applied.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The unemployment benefit statement on file sets the document extension month of the relief installment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Hand the catch-up payment tool to the patient so she can pay the catch-up herself.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the user unlock/call pair; no DB effect; the catch-up payment is the patient's own payment.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The patient pays the catch-up payment by debit card against missed installment 8, bringing the plan back to active.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: plans_ext_catch_up_payment computes the amount; the relief installment may not be set on the past-due plan until this arrears payment is on the ledger, and it lowers the carried balance the later installments spread.

Basis: the docstring asks for 'the number of the missed installment this payment settles, copied from the missed-installment line on the plan's activity'; the catch-up rule posts the payment 'as an arrears payment against the plan's latest missed installment'. The latest missed line is initial_state.plan_transactions.c2d2de1a-8426-49b7-b27b-1a1f1bacadf9 (installment_number 8, recorded 2026-10-06). factor_trace: catch_up_credit_selection (method): 2 missed lines in the last 12 whole months (initial_state.plan_transactions.9e43d815-0ca2-42c8-8a7c-c6be06fc3667 2026-05-06, initial_state.plan_transactions.c2d2de1a-8426-49b7-b27b-1a1f1bacadf9 2026-10-06) and installments drawn automatically from a bank account -> only the largest single extra-principal payment posted against the latest missed installment (installment 8) counts: initial_state.plan_transactions.d75c18ff-a645-45b4-b776-ecf5cb3e80a5 75.00 (2026-10-09) rather than initial_state.plan_transactions.80a44321-39e7-41af-87cc-d18752490fb0 40.00 (2026-10-12). Baseline (all of them, 115.00) gives 92.50. Near-miss: initial_state.plan_transactions.c4ab43e2-677e-4af3-8848-9d2bfda8e67d 40.00 of 2026-08-10 and initial_state.plan_transactions.80d575ce-a36b-47e5-9be0-dbeb62418449 125.00 of 2026-05-29 carry no installment number (posted while the plan was current) and never count.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The relief installment and the add-on down payment are both prerequisites of the root and are not ordered with respect to each other. They commute: the relief installment reads its carried balance with the acceptance down payment taken from the plan record (down_payment_amount = 370.00), so a later down-payment line does not enter it, and the add-on down payment reads only missed lines, scheduled-payment counts, the enrolled-invoice count, the award, the open invoice and the latest scheduled payment method, none of which the relief installment writes. Replaying the gold with the two unlock/call pairs swapped (add-on down payment at steps 13-14, relief installment at steps 15-16) gives the add-on down payment 9.50 and the relief installment 35.00 again, and the terminal DB hash is identical in both orders (c826a348...). The catch-up payment must precede the relief installment (its prerequisite edge) and does not interact with the add-on down payment either (the catch-up credit counts only additional_principal lines carrying the missed installment number; the add-on down payment counts missed lines, which the catch-up does not write).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the relief installment leaves installment_amount at 185.00 = the acceptance installment; the added invoice is then spread over the term count (10 - 1 held) and the added-invoice installment becomes 185.00 + 233.70 / 9 = 210.97 instead of 51.69.
Skipping the add-on down payment leaves n_addon_down at 0.00; the added-invoice installment becomes 35.00 + 243.20 / 14 = 52.37 instead of 51.69, and the terminal ledger lacks the down-payment line.

Skipping the catch-up payment leaves the carried balance at 635.00 and the plan past_due; the relief installment becomes 635.00 / 15 = 42.33 instead of 35.00 (and the added-invoice installment 48.75 instead of 51.69); the terminal ledger lacks the arrears line and keeps status past_due.
